title: Design System: Alucard
scope: The watch landing world: frontend/app/page.tsx, frontend/components/watch/ (WatchLanding.tsx, Movement.tsx, watch.css), fonts in frontend/app/layout.tsx, frontend/app/icon.svg. Tokens are CSS custom properties scoped to .w-page in watch.css. The rest of the app (other frontend/components and frontend/app/globals.css) still carries an older, separate look that this world will replace; it is out of scope for this record.

ruby.note: #ff9aa9 is the jewel highlight inside drawings only.

blued-steel.note: Darker steps are screw rims and slots inside the movement drawing.

brass.note: Wheel fill, chaton, spoke. Literal values inside watch.css and icon.svg, no custom property.

enamel.note: Used as a literal (#fbfbfc) in watch.css and WatchLanding.tsx; not yet a custom property.

title.purpose: Statement terms in definition lists; certificate figures at 26px.

lead.purpose: Hero paragraph and the plain-words rule sentence.

label.purpose: Fieldset legends and the certificate issuing line; the same face in gilt engraves the drawings.

dial-numeral.purpose: Dial scale, subdial values, status window.

shadows.name: case-drop
shadows.purpose: Outer case of every watch drawing, and only there.

shadows.name: hairline-outline
shadows.purpose: Ghost buttons, step buttons, select; becomes inset 0 0 0 1px #1b1d22 on hover.

shadows.name: certificate-border
shadows.purpose: Double engraved rule around the certificate.

motion.name: ease-out-mech
motion.purpose: Button press (0.15s) and the hero movement entrance (1.4s, from scale 0.96 and -6deg).

motion.name: ease-swing
motion.purpose: Balance wheel (0.3s per swing, ±110deg, alternate), hairspring breathing, rotor (14s, -70 to 250deg).

motion.name: wheel-train
motion.value: linear infinite rotation, per-wheel period from gear ratio; escape wheel steps(150)

motion.name: setpoint-spring
motion.purpose: Ruby set-point hand driven by the crown.

motion.name: scroll-spring
motion.purpose: Smooths replay scroll progress; first 18% flips the watch rotateY 180 to 0.

motion.name: state-fade
motion.purpose: Button background, colour and outline transitions.

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.purpose: All mechanism animation stops; replay shows its final state without pinning.

breakpoints.name: lg
breakpoints.note: Two-column split, pinned replay, full-size instruments.

narrative.overview:
Alucard is drawn as a plate from a technical catalogue of fine watchmaking: cool white paper, graphite linework, and a working automatic movement whose bridges are engraved with the parts of a rule. The object does the explaining. Each viewport holds one drawn instrument (the movement, the dial, the caseback, the certificate) beside a short column of plain prose, and everything that moves moves the way a mechanism moves: wheels at their gear ratios, a balance swinging, hands that spring to a value and settle.

Density is low and deliberate. Sections are separated by a single hairline and long vertical air, never by cards or tinted panels. Colour is almost entirely neutral graphite on paper; the warmth comes from material colours inside the drawings (gilt, brass, blued screws), and a single ruby red marks jewels and the moment a rule acts. Type pairs a tight grotesque for statements with an engraved Roman capital for labels, the way a dial pairs numerals with its signature.

This world was built to refuse the DeFi landing default: no dark hero, no gradient glow, no glass panels, no stat rows, no feature-card grids.
keyCharacteristics: Cool paper ground with graphite ink; depth from linework, not fills.
One drawn instrument per viewport, rendered as authored SVG, never as a raster or 3D render.
Ruby is scarce and semantic: jewels, the stop, the set point, and "it ran".
Engraved small capitals label the drawings; prose stays sentence case.
Motion is mechanical only and stops entirely under reduced motion.

rules.name: The One Jewel Rule
rules.body: Ruby marks a pivot or the moment a rule acts. If removing the red would not lose meaning, it should not be red.

rules.name: The Material Colour Rule
rules.body: Gilt, brass and blued steel belong to the drawn mechanism. They never fill a button, a band, or a panel.

rules.name: The Engraving Rule
rules.body: Spaced capitals are reserved for things that would be engraved on a movement: part names, the signature, legends that name a mechanism (When, Then). Headlines and prose are always sentence case.

rules.name: The Plain Words Rule
rules.body: Contract field names appear only in Geist Mono and only behind an explicit reveal. The visible layer is plain English.

rules.name: The One Object Rule
rules.body: A viewport holds one drawn instrument. Never place two drawings side by side or add supporting graphics beside one.

rules.name: The Paper Is Flat Rule
rules.body: Bands and text blocks never float. Only the watch object and the one action that opens the app carry a shadow.

dos: Do keep one drawn instrument per viewport, at a fixed column width beside fluid prose.
Do reserve ruby for jewels, the stop, the set point, "RAN", focus, selection and the certificate's results.
Do separate sections with a single hairline and 112px of padding; alternate with the enamel band, not with boxes.
Do set engraving in Marcellus capitals with wide tracking (0.22em in HTML, 0.3em or more inside drawings).

Do animate only as a mechanism would: continuous rotation at gear ratios, oscillation, springs that settle, and the scroll-driven turn-over. Stop all of it under reduced motion and show the final state.
Do pair every drag interaction (the crown) with keyboard steps and visible buttons.
Do keep numerals tabular everywhere a value changes.
donts: Don't use a dark hero, gradient glow, glass panels, stat rows or feature-card grids.
Don't fill buttons, bands or panels with gilt, brass or blued steel.
Don't render the mechanism as a raster, photo or 3D model; it is drawn linework.
Don't set headlines or prose in capitals; capitals are engraving.
Don't show contract field names outside the mono reveal.
Don't add shadows to bands, rows or text blocks; only the case and the primary button carry one.
